channel.title: Moses Agentic: Technology news for business
channel.description: Reputable technology news, summarized for business owners.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with lower costs per task for heavy and everyday work
item.description: OpenAI released two new models on November 17, 2026. GPT-6.2 Astra is built for demanding professional work such as documents, spreadsheets, code and research; GPT-6.2 Sol is a cheaper model for everyday tasks and multistep workflows. Both are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex on paid plans and in the API, priced at $8 and $40 per million input and output tokens for Astra and $2 and $10 for Sol. OpenAI says Astra completes a typical task for under a third of what its predecessor cost. On November 23, a Sol-based version began rolling out to the regular Chat tab, including Business plans.

item.title: OpenAI pilots OpenWorks, free in-person AI help for independently owned U.S. small businesses
item.description: OpenAI started a pilot called OpenWorks on November 23, 2026 that pays local partners to help independently owned U.S. small businesses put AI to work, at no cost to the owner. Participating businesses also get three months of ChatGPT Business. Software and SaaS firms, venture-backed companies and private-equity-owned businesses are excluded; nonprofits and faith-based groups may apply. Partners are contractors who receive a stipend of up to $8,000 a month and must spend at least four days a month working in person with local businesses. The pilot starts in a limited set of U.S. communities, and owners elsewhere can register interest. OpenAI's help page does not say what happens after the free three months.

item.title: New York bans the sale of AI chatbot toys for five years, starting in about 90 days
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a law on November 24, 2026 (S.9408A/A.11144B) that places a five-year moratorium on making, distributing and selling toys in the state with built-in AI chatbots, such as talking plush animals, dolls and robots that hold open-ended conversations with children over the internet. The law takes effect 90 days after signing, so it does not apply this holiday season. Violations carry civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day, enforced by the state Attorney General. The state pointed to consumer-watchdog testing in which some of these toys raised unsafe topics with children.

item.title: OpenAI lets businesses claim profiles in ChatGPT and publish their own agents there
item.description: OpenAI opened a beta Business Hub where companies can claim a profile inside ChatGPT and see how people engage with it. Eligible ecommerce and online service businesses can also publish a business agent that answers customer questions inside ChatGPT, and those agents can be promoted through ChatGPT ads. On November 19 OpenAI extended eligibility to businesses outside the U.S. TechCrunch describes the move as a step toward making ChatGPT work more like a search and discovery engine for local and online businesses.

item.title: New York's AI safety law starts putting large AI developers under state oversight
item.description: New York's RAISE Act, which covers the largest AI model developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, is moving into effect, with developers required to register with the state by January 1, 2027. The law asks these companies to publish safety plans and report serious incidents, and it allows large penalties for violations. TechCrunch notes that California and Illinois have similar rules, while federal officials are pushing to limit how far states can regulate AI development.

item.title: Gartner: about one in five service leaders cut support staff because of AI, and many may rehire
item.description: A Gartner survey of customer service and support leaders found that 21 percent have reduced the number of human support agents because of AI. Most have not. Gartner also predicts that half of the companies that cut service staff because of AI will hire people back by 2027, as customers still expect a person for complex or sensitive issues and AI tools fall short of full replacement.

item.title: Study of 3,662 property managers: AI use reaches 58 percent, but under half see it in the bottom line
item.description: AppFolio and the Institute of Real Estate Management released AI Insights 2026 on November 5, 2026, a survey of 3,662 real estate management professionals taken May 7 to June 7, 2026. AI use in the job rose from 21 percent in 2023 to 58 percent, the first time a majority reported using it, and the smallest firms have passed 50 percent. Among users, 85 percent report productivity gains but only 48 percent report a positive effect on net operating income. Only 8 percent of organizations have a written AI policy and 74 percent of professionals have had no formal AI training. Concern is high: 92 percent worry about AI-related cybersecurity and 93 percent about AI-faked applicant documents.

item.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot gets a long-running Autopilot agent, shared workspaces and a spend dashboard for agents
item.description: At its Ignite conference on November 17, 2026, Microsoft described the next version of Copilot for work: Autopilot, an agent that keeps running recurring tasks on its own; Copilot Code, which builds dashboards, trackers and small apps from plain-language instructions; and Copilot Workspaces, where people and agents share the same files and context. For managers, Agent 365 Business Analytics is meant to show what the company's AI is costing and delivering, and Agent 365 policies will be enforced on every Windows device. Microsoft IQ connects agents to company knowledge, with a Salesforce plugin in preview. Microsoft did not give prices or dates for most of these in the announcement.

item.title: FBI: poisoned search results and hacked WordPress sites led to more than $28 million in ransom payments
item.description: The FBI issued an alert on November 16, 2026 about Gootloader, malware that reaches businesses through ordinary web searches. Criminals plant pages on hacked WordPress sites that rank for narrow searches, such as a specific contract clause, and the visitor downloads a file that opens the door for ransomware. As of October 2026 the FBI counted more than 1,000 infected WordPress sites, 216 domains run by the operator, and over $28 million in ransom payments. Recent targeting has focused on lawyers, in-house counsel and legal technology buyers. The alert tells organizations what to do if a staff member downloaded or opened such a file, and recommends reviewing incident response plans.

item.title: Microsoft says a network upgrade, not Copilot, caused the Microsoft 365 outage
item.description: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted for many businesses starting November 12, 2026, and service came back gradually over the following days. Microsoft's preliminary explanation points to a hidden bug in the systems that set up secure connections, which surfaced when traffic shifted during network maintenance and upgrades. The company said its Copilot assistant did not cause the outage and that it saw no sign of malicious activity.

item.title: Infoblox confirms a security incident traced to an outside vendor
item.description: Infoblox, a company that sells network security products, confirmed that someone gained unauthorized access to certain company information. A spokesperson told TechCrunch the access came through a compromised third-party data migration vendor and that the company is investigating. The incident is a reminder that a breach can start with a supplier and not with the company itself.

item.title: Apple services including the App Store and Apple Music go down; Apple points to an internal update
item.description: Several Apple services stopped working for part of November 17, 2026. Apple's status page listed full outages for Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare, and reports named iCloud among the services hit. Apple attributed the problem to an internal update and said it was not the result of a cyberattack. The outage followed a Microsoft 365 disruption the week before.
